name: Guselkumab
route_note: Subcutaneous injection every 8 weeks after loading; IV or SC induction for IBD
originator: Janssen, from an antibody discovered with MorphoSys HuCAL technology

discovery.note: Fully human IgG1λ antibody against IL-23 p19 selected from MorphoSys's HuCAL phage library. Year is the priority date of the Centocor human anti-IL-23 antibody patent (US 7,935,344).

tagline: First IL-23 p19-selective antibody approved, for psoriasis, PsA and IBD
summary: Guselkumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody that selectively inhibits interleukin-23 by binding its p19 subunit. It was the first IL-23-selective drug approved, for plaque psoriasis in 2017, and is now also used for psoriatic arthritis, ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease.
mechanism: Guselkumab binds the p19 subunit of IL-23, preventing it from binding its receptor and blocking downstream JAK–STAT signalling that maintains Th17 responses.
Its Fc region binds CD64 (FcγRI), which is expressed on IL-23-producing myeloid cells; this may let guselkumab capture IL-23 at its cellular source.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in July for plaque psoriasis, the first IL-23 p19 inhibitor; EU approval in November.

history.title: ECLIPSE
history.detail: Guselkumab is superior to secukinumab at week 48 in psoriasis.

history.title: Ulcerative colitis
history.detail: FDA approves guselkumab for UC in September (QUASAR).

history.title: Crohn's disease
history.detail: Approved for Crohn's disease, with both IV and subcutaneous induction options.

pk.metabolism: Proteolytic catabolism to peptides and amino acids (no CYP metabolism)
pk.excretion: Not renally excreted as intact antibody; cleared by catabolism and target-mediated uptake

facts: Guselkumab was the first approved antibody selective for IL-23 rather than shared IL-12/IL-23 p40.
It can be self-injected with a patient-controlled injector.
